newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends quietly in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends quietly in thin trade.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market finished quietly on Friday with most of the major consumers sidelined and players looking for direction next week, dealers said.
"The volume today and the past three days has not been that heavy. Goodyear's sidelined. So were all the major consumers. It's very quiet," a dealer said.
"We tried issuing prices this afternoon, but nobody was hitting us. It's really very quiet," another dealer said.
The only substantial action was seen in forward months of TSR20 rubber, where total trade reached about 1,800 tonnes.
Dealers said the virtually flat level of rubber prices in Tokyo, where the benchmark November contract closed 0.1 yen up at 138.1, provided little inspiration to the market.
"There's really no news in the market. The Thai news on the government intervening in the market has already been digested by the trade," a dealer said.

At 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 115.50 U.S. cents a kg from 115.00 cents. July RSS1 was indicated at 165.25 Singapore cents (US$1.15) a kg from 164.75 cents. August TSR20 was seen at 156.50 Singapore cents (US$1.09) a kg from the previous 157.00 cents. - (S$1.43 = US$1) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
